papers.title: Unraveling the pathogenic mechanisms of osteoarthritis and obesity: An integration of GWAS, cellular specificity, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically elucidate the shared and specific genetic basis of osteoarthritis (OA) and obesity by integrating large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, cross-tissue quantitative trait loci (QTLs), and single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data.
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, QTL, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data to identify shared and tissue-specific genetic mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis and obesity, revealing potential common pathogenic pathways. The findings provide a systematic view of how genetic risk variants may act in specific cell types and spatial contexts to contribute to both diseases.

papers.title: A multi-omics integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies and validates a 16-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition prognostic signature in tongue squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes, highlighting the critical need for dependable prognostic indicators. The epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a fundamental biological process driving cancer progression. This study aimed to develop and independently validate an EMT-associated gene expression signature for predicting prognosis in TSCC through a multi-omics strategy.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a 16-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) prognostic signature for tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) by integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomics. The signature independently predicts patient outcomes, offering a potentially reliable clinical tool for risk stratification in this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: AI-Guided Long Non-Coding RNA Target Discovery for Precision Medicine: Integrating GWAS, Multi-Omics, Experimental Validation, and RNA Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Precision medicine requires translation of genetic and molecular variation into clinically actionable therapeutic targets. However, many disease-associated signals identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) reside in non-coding regulatory regions, making biological interpretation and therapeutic prioritization difficult. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are regulatory molecules with growing relevance to disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and RNA-based therapeutics. This review presents a translational framework for AI-guided lncRNA t
papers.summary: This review proposes a translational framework that integrates GWAS, multi-omics data, experimental validation, and AI-guided approaches to identify long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as therapeutic targets for precision medicine. It highlights the challenges of interpreting non-coding disease-associated variants and outlines how AI can prioritize lncRNAs for RNA-based therapeutics, biomarker discovery, and patient stratification.

papers.title: Scale-Aware Compositional Inference Improves Reproducibility and Uncovers Convergent Aging Programs in Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables analysis of molecular organization with anatomical context. Existing spatial differential expression methods are restricted to within-sample inference, forcing between-sample comparisons to rely on approaches adapted from single-cell RNA-seq. Here, we establish a scale-aware inference framework for spatial differential expression by modeling compositional constraints and variation in total RNA abundance rather than removing them through normalization, enabling calibrated between-sample inference at cell-level resolution. Our method produces more reliable results
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new statistical framework for spatial transcriptomics that models compositional constraints and total RNA abundance directly, rather than relying on normalization, enabling calibrated between-sample differential expression at cell-level resolution. The method improves reproducibility and uncovers convergent aging programs, addressing a key limitation of existing spatial differential expression approaches.

papers.title: High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Pathological Microregion-Specific Luminal Subset Plasticity and Core Signaling Networks Underlying Prostate Cancer Malignancy.
papers.abstract: Background: Prostate cancer (PCa) exhibits strong multidimensional heterogeneity. The dynamic evolution of Luminal subsets and their crosstalk with the tumor microenvironment (TME) during malignant progression remain poorly understood. Conventional single-cell transcriptomics lacks spatial context, while low-resolution spatial technologies cannot resolve single-cell and subcellular interactions. This study aimed to map a high-resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas to characterize Luminal subset heterogeneity and stromal crosstalk across progressive PCa lesions. Methods: We used high-resolutio
papers.summary: This study uses high-resolution spatial transcriptomics to map prostate cancer lesions, revealing that specific luminal cell subsets exhibit plasticity and interact with the tumor microenvironment in distinct pathological microregions. The findings identify core signaling networks that may drive prostate cancer malignancy, offering new insights into the spatial organization of tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: GRAIL-heart: A graph attention network for inferring ligand-receptor interactions in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication through ligand-receptor (L-R) interactions orchestrates cardiac development, homeostasis, and disease progression, yet existing computational methods cannot infer directional signalling networks or distinguish causal from correlational interactions in spatial transcriptomics data. We present GRAIL-Heart, a graph-attention-based framework that integrates spatial tissue topology with multi-task learning to predict context-dependent L-R interactions, reconstruct gene expression, and infer causal signalling pathways. Validated on 42,654 cells across six cardiac regions from
papers.summary: GRAIL-heart is a new graph attention network that infers ligand-receptor interactions from spatial transcriptomics data, incorporating spatial topology and multi-task learning to predict directional signaling and distinguish causal from correlational interactions. Validated on cardiac tissue, it offers a more context-aware approach to studying cell-cell communication.

papers.title: Protocol to characterize tumor microenvironment in a diffuse midline glioma mouse model using multi-omics approach on sequential sections.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) tumors form complex tumor-immune microenvironments with marked cellular heterogeneity. Here, we present a protocol to generate orthotopic DMG tumors in immunocompetent neonatal mice and to spatially characterize the tumor ecosystem using a multi-omics workflow on sequential brain sections. We detail procedures for brain freezing, cryosectioning, single-nuclei RNA sequencing, and Visium spatial transcriptomics. We then describe steps for cyclic immunofluorescence and integrative computational analysis to resolve cellular states and spatial organization. For complete
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes a multi-omics workflow to characterize the tumor microenvironment in a diffuse midline glioma (DMG) mouse model, combining single-nuclei RNA sequencing, Visium spatial transcriptomics, and cyclic immunofluorescence on sequential brain sections. It provides detailed steps for generating orthotopic tumors in immunocompetent neonatal mice and integrating computational analyses to resolve cellular states and spatial organization. This offers a comprehensive resource for studying DMG tumor-immune interactions.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals the FA9-VAP Module Regulating Fatty Acid Accumulation in Soybean Seeds.
papers.abstract: As a major commercial legume crop, soybean ranks among the world's most significant sources of edible oil and plant protein. We previously identified a SEIPIN homologue (FA9) at the fatty acid 9 locus that promotes fatty acid accumulation in soybean. To examine the detailed molecular mechanisms by which FA9 regulates lipid metabolism, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (stRNA-seq) of wild-type and FA9-knockout soybean seeds at the late maturity stage. scRNA-seq analysis identified 26 transcriptional clusters and revealed the spatial distribution of
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to uncover a FA9-VAP module that regulates fatty acid accumulation in soybean seeds, providing detailed molecular insights into lipid metabolism in this crop. The findings could inform strategies for improving oil content in soybean.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell sequencing and machine learning to identify specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets and chronic inflammation as key drivers of poor outcomes in ovarian cancer, particularly in residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight potential targets for improving treatment response.

papers.title: Overactivation of SHH signaling induces a cascade of dedifferentiation and oncogenesis in a new mouse model for choroid plexus carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Choroid Plexus tumors constitute 10-20% of brain tumors in infancy. Among these, Choroid Plexus Carcinomas (CPC) are highly aggressive and result in poor survival. Details on tumor initiation and oncogenic events remain largely unknown, aside from a high prevalence of TP53 mutations and marked chromosomal instability. We generated hGFAP-cre::lsl-MYCN::lsl-Gli2(N)::Tp53fl/fl mice with recombination activity from embryonic day 13.5 onwards in CNS cells, leading to MYCN and Gli2 activation as well as TP53 inactivation. 84% of the mice developed ventricular tumors within 18 days of life, resemblin
papers.summary: This study introduces a new mouse model for choroid plexus carcinoma (CPC) by activating SHH signaling (via Gli2) alongside MYCN overexpression and TP53 loss, which rapidly induces ventricular tumors resembling human CPC. The findings demonstrate that overactivation of the SHH pathway drives a cascade of dedifferentiation and oncogenesis, providing a valuable tool for studying CPC initiation and progression.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals D2-associated synaptic transcriptional attenuation in the chronically stressed dorsal striatum.
papers.abstract: Chronic stress alters striatal functions involved in motivation, action selection, and behavioral adaptation, yet cell-type-associated transcriptional organization in the dorsal striatum remains unclear. We used RNAscope-guided GeoMx spatial transcriptomics to compare D1 and D2 neuronal compartments in matched dorsal striatal regions after chronic restraint stress (CRS). CRS engaged both populations, producing CRS-responsive gene sets in both D1- and D2-enriched compartments. Gene set enrichment analysis revealed partially overlapping CRS-associated pathway attenuation in both compartments, in
papers.summary: This study uses RNAscope-guided GeoMx spatial transcriptomics to profile D1 and D2 medium spiny neurons in the dorsal striatum after chronic restraint stress, revealing that chronic stress induces transcriptional attenuation in both compartments, with D2 neurons showing particularly pronounced synaptic gene downregulation. The findings provide cell-type-resolved insights into how stress disrupts striatal circuits, linking D2-specific transcriptional changes to stress-related behavioral deficits.

papers.title: Tumor-Intrinsic DNA Damage Signaling Is Associated with MHC-I Expression and CD8 Cytotoxic T-Cell Engagement in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by marked immune microenvironment heterogeneity and variable chemotherapy response, yet the epithelial transcriptional programs governing cytotoxic immune activation remain poorly understood. We performed an exploratory, integrative analysis using single-cell RNA sequencing of 31,962 cells from eight TNBC patients operationally stratified into Good and Bad Prognosis groups based on pathological lymphoid infiltration, a discovery grouping subsequently validated against pathological complete response (pCR) in three independent bulk RNA-seq co
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of TNBC tumors to show that tumor-intrinsic DNA damage signaling is linked to higher MHC-I expression and greater CD8+ T-cell engagement, suggesting a mechanism by which tumor cells may promote cytotoxic immune responses. The findings could help stratify TNBC patients by prognosis and response to therapy.

papers.title: Targeting a candidate stromal immune checkpoint: a cellular senescence signature identifies COMP⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts associated with CD8⁺ T-cell exclusion via a predicted COMP-CD47 axis in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Resistance to immunotherapy in colorectal cancer (CRC) is closely linked to an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME), in which cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key regulators. Cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) are increasingly recognised as drivers of CAF activity, yet their systematic prognostic and immunomodulatory value in CRC remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study identifies a cellular senescence signature in colorectal cancer that defines a specific population of COMP⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). These COMP⁺ CAFs are associated with CD8⁺ T-cell exclusion, likely through a predicted COMP-CD47 immune checkpoint axis, offering a potential new target for immunotherapy.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific damage scores reveal kidney and liver disease trajectories in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Degenerative diseases progress through gradual cell-intrinsic damage that is difficult to resolve with bulk transcriptomics or discrete cell-state analysis. We introduce a generalizable single-cell and spatial transcriptomics framework that quantifies continuous damage trajectories in vivo using cell-type-specific scores. Applied to chronic kidney disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the podocyte damage score (PDS) and hepatocyte damage score (HDS) place individual podocytes and hepatocytes on a health-to-damage axis. Across mouse and human single-cell RNA sequ
papers.summary: This paper introduces a generalizable computational framework that quantifies continuous cell-intrinsic damage trajectories from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data, using cell-type-specific scores. Applied to chronic kidney disease and metabolic liver disease, the framework places individual cells on a health-to-damage axis, revealing disease progression across mouse and human samples.

papers.title: POSTN⁺ CAF-SPP1⁺ macrophage crosstalk is associated with immune exclusion and poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly lethal malignancy in which the tumor microenvironment (TME) plays an important role in disease progression and therapeutic resistance. However, the spatial organization and molecular basis of stromal-immune interactions in LUAD remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study identifies a specific crosstalk between POSTN⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1⁺ macrophages in lung adenocarcinoma that is associated with immune exclusion and poor prognosis. The findings suggest that this stromal-immune interaction may contribute to therapeutic resistance and highlight potential targets for improving immunotherapy response.

papers.title: Circulating Homocysteine and Choroid Plexus Volume Across the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: Cross-Sectional and Progression-Related Associations.
papers.abstract: Elevated plasma homocysteine (HCY) is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its relationship with structural brain changes across the AD continuum remains unclear. The choroid plexus (CP) regulates cerebrospinal fluid homeostasis and may interface with peripheral metabolic signals. Whether HCY relates to CP structural alterations and disease progression remains unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates the link between elevated blood homocysteine levels and choroid plexus volume changes across the Alzheimer's disease spectrum, finding associations that may relate to disease progression. The results suggest that homocysteine could influence brain structures involved in cerebrospinal fluid regulation, offering a potential marker for AD progression.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent spatial transcriptomics methods for analyzing cell-cell communication (CCC), organizing them into three groups based on their analytical frameworks: network inference at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory module identification. It provides a structured overview to help researchers select appropriate methods for their biological questions.

papers.title: A Neuro-Immune Score Defines a Stromal-Neural and Immune-Segregated Microenvironment Associated with Poor Prognosis in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer progression and therapeutic response are determined not only by tumor-intrinsic programs but also by neural, stromal, and immune components of the tumor microenvironment. However, biologically interpretable transcriptomic scores that jointly capture neural/stromal remodeling and immune activation remain limited. We developed a neuro-immune score (NIS), defined as the neural/stromal module score minus the immune activation module score. NIS was constructed using the combined TCGA-COAD/READ colorectal cancer cohort and externally evaluated in independent Gene Expression Omnibus
papers.summary: The authors developed a neuro-immune score (NIS) that captures the balance between neural/stromal remodeling and immune activation in the colorectal cancer microenvironment. They found that a high NIS, indicating a stromal-neural enriched and immune-segregated microenvironment, is associated with poor prognosis, providing a biologically interpretable transcriptomic score with potential clinical utility.

papers.title: Coordinated Expression of ADC Targets ERBB2, TACSTD2, and NECTIN4 in Bladder Cancer: A Multi-Scale Transcriptomic and Proteomic Landscape Analysis.
papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) targeting HER2 (encoded by ERBB2), Trop2 (TACSTD2), and Nectin-4 (NECTIN4) have demonstrated clinical activity in bladder cancer. However, the co-expression relationships among these three targets at both the transcriptomic and protein levels, and their spatial organization within the tumor microenvironment, remain incompletely characterized. To address this, we performed a multi-platform, multi-resolution analysis integrating ten bulk RNA-seq datasets (n = 1628 samples), six spatial transcriptomics datasets (10x Visium and Visium HD, n = 31 specimens), and mult
papers.summary: This study provides a multi-scale analysis of the expression of three ADC targets (ERBB2, TACSTD2, NECTIN4) in bladder cancer, integrating bulk RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and proteomics. The findings reveal coordinated expression patterns and spatial organization within the tumor microenvironment, which could inform patient selection and combination strategies for ADC therapies.

papers.title: DSG2 Expression Marks a Stromal-Immune Organizational State in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immune exclusion in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) limits immunotherapy efficacy, yet the molecular determinants of stromal-immune organization remain incompletely characterized. The desmosomal cadherin DSG2 is highly expressed in squamous epithelium; its role in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) is unknown.
papers.summary: This study identifies DSG2 expression as a marker of a specific stromal-immune organizational state in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), potentially influencing immune exclusion and immunotherapy response. The findings suggest that DSG2 may play a role in shaping the tumor microenvironment, offering a new avenue for understanding and targeting immune resistance in HNSCC.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. It reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the switch between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Omics Technologies in Rice Abiotic Stress Biology: A Methodological Review.
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses-drought, salinity, extreme temperature, flooding, and heavy-metal toxicity-constrain rice (Oryza sativa L.) yield worldwide, and the cellular programmes underlying them are unevenly distributed across cell types that bulk-tissue assays average together. This review examines, from a methodological standpoint, what single-cell and spatial omics technologies can and cannot establish about rice abiotic stress biology. We first define the modality space: single-cell omics measures RNA, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, protein, or metabolite features at the resolution of in
papers.summary: This methodological review evaluates the current and potential applications of single-cell and spatial omics technologies in studying rice responses to abiotic stresses such as drought, salinity, and temperature extremes. It highlights how these approaches can reveal cell-type-specific programs that bulk assays miss, while also discussing their limitations and future directions for rice research.

papers.title: Spatial Immune Coding in Tumor-Draining Lymph Nodes: Functional Compartmentalization of Immune Activation and Immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are important immune organs linking primary tumors with systemic immune responses. They support tumor antigen presentation, T-cell priming, and effector immune responses, but under sustained tumor influence they can also be remodeled into microenvironments that promote immune escape and metastatic colonization. Conventional methods, including flow cytometry, bulk RNA sequencing, and routine immunohistochemistry, have advanced our understanding of TDLN immunity but cannot simultaneously preserve tissue architecture, cell identity, and spatial cell-cell relatio
papers.summary: This review discusses the functional compartmentalization of tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs), highlighting how they can support both immune activation and immunosuppression depending on spatial organization. It emphasizes the need for spatial-omics technologies to capture the architecture and cell-cell interactions that conventional methods miss, offering a framework for understanding TDLN immunity and potential therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors. It identifies specific microbial taxa and inflammatory mediators that may influence tumor risk, highlighting the gut-immune-brain axis as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: VIDEO-Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization: a tool for integrating and visualizing chromatin accessibility, in vivo transcription factor binding and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes.
papers.abstract: Dissecting gene regulation today relies on many genomic assays-including transcriptional output from RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, and transcription factor (TF) binding from ChIP-seq. Whereas numerous tools exist for each modality and some integrate data across modalities, few allow researchers to interactively explore and visualize how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in a tissue-specific context. Here we introduce VIDEO (Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization), a web-based analysis tool that enables visual
papers.summary: VIDEO is a new web-based tool that integrates and visualizes chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and motif occurrence with tissue-specific gene expression data in Drosophila. It allows researchers to interactively explore how TF binding motifs relate to transcriptional activity and chromatin state, filling a gap in existing genomic analysis tools.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Sequencing Analysis Identifies an Aging-Related Gene Signature for Prognosis in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence exerts a complex influence on BRCA progression and TME remodeling. However, the specific roles of ASIGs in regulating the TME and determining patient outcomes remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-sequencing data from breast cancer (BRCA) patients to identify an aging-related gene signature (ASIGs) that is associated with tumor microenvironment remodeling and patient prognosis. The authors develop a prognostic gene signature that could help stratify patients by risk, highlighting the role of cellular senescence in BRCA outcomes.

papers.title: SPIDER: spatially integrated denoising via embedding regularization with single cell supervision.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies profile gene expression while preserving tissue architecture, enabling the study of spatial cellular organization and microenvironmental interactions. However, raw ST data are heavily affected by technical noise, sparsity, and dropout events, which obscure true biological signals and hinder downstream analyses. While recent denoising methods incorporate spatial neighborhood information, they lack explicit supervision due to missing cell-type annotations in ST data. To address this challenge, we introduce SPIDER, a semi-supervised framework that leverag
papers.summary: SPIDER is a new semi-supervised framework for denoising spatial transcriptomics data that integrates single-cell RNA-seq data as supervision to overcome the lack of cell-type annotations in spatial data. By using embedding regularization, it effectively reduces technical noise and dropout while preserving spatial structure, improving downstream analyses.

papers.title: ScanNet: Single-cell annotation informed by transcriptional regulation Network via iterative heterogeneous graph learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate annotation of cell types in single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular identities. The transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), which map the regulatory relationships between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes (TGs), capture the molecular dependencies underlying transcriptional programs. However, most existing cell type annotation methods do not fully exploit this regulatory information. Therefore, we introduce ScanNet, a Single cell annotation method informed by transcriptional regulation Network, to integrate prior
papers.summary: ScanNet is a new computational method that improves single-cell RNA-seq cell type annotation by integrating transcriptional regulatory network information through iterative heterogeneous graph learning. It outperforms existing methods by leveraging regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes, providing more accurate cell type identification.

papers.title: Multiscale learning of gene network-driven phenotypic dynamics of single cells.
papers.abstract: Understanding how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) dynamically orchestrate cell fate emergence remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present GRNvelo, a computational framework that reconstructs multiscale cell fate dynamics by integrating GRNs with phenotypic dynamics from temporal single-cell RNA-seq data. GRNvelo establishes a biologically interpretable and mathematically rigorous multiscale model that couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with nonlocal cell growth-mediated population dynamics. To operationalize this model, GRNvelo devises a two-phase cooperative optimization algorithm
papers.summary: GRNvelo is a new computational framework that integrates gene regulatory networks with temporal single-cell RNA-seq data to reconstruct multiscale cell fate dynamics. It couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with population-level growth dynamics using a two-phase optimization algorithm, providing a biologically interpretable model of how gene networks orchestrate cell fate emergence.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper describes a rapid, ligand-based protocol for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into granulosa-like cells that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a valuable in vitro model for studying human ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. The protocol's effectiveness was validated using single-cell RNA-sequencing, which confirmed the expression of lineage markers and steroidogenic pathway genes.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Analyses Link Arachidonic Acid Metabolic Reprogramming to Proneural-to-Mesenchymal State Transition in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glioblastoma (GBM) is widely recognised as a highly aggressive form of malignant tumour arising within the central nervous system. The proneural-to-mesenchymal (PN-MES) state transition is a key process underlying malignant progression and therapeutic resistance. The present study was designed to elucidate the association between the PN-MES transition and arachidonic acid (AA) metabolic reprogramming in GBM. Methods: We integrated four public single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts, two spatial transcriptomic cohorts, and three bulk RNA-sequencing cohorts for GBM. By combinin
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data from glioblastoma (GBM) patients to link arachidonic acid (AA) metabolic reprogramming with the proneural-to-mesenchymal (PN-MES) state transition, a key driver of malignancy and therapy resistance. The findings suggest that AA metabolism is upregulated in mesenchymal-like tumor cells and may play a role in driving the PN-MES transition, offering potential new therapeutic targets.

papers.title: SlotDeconv: spatial transcriptomics deconvolution via diversity-constrained prototype learning and spatial refinement.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression in intact tissues. In spot-based ST assays, each spot can contain mixtures of multiple cell types. Deconvolution is particularly challenging when closely related cell subtypes share highly similar expression profiles and when spatial context is underutilized during proportion estimation.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SlotDeconv, a new computational method for deconvolving cell types in spatial transcriptomics data. It uses diversity-constrained prototype learning to distinguish closely related cell subtypes and incorporates spatial refinement to improve proportion estimates, addressing key limitations of existing approaches.

papers.title: Disruption of hippocampal upstream regulators of mTOR and insulin pathways in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease neuropathology: Preliminary observations.
papers.abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is caused by a complete or partial trisomy of chromosome 21, resulting in variable intellectual disabilities and a high risk for early-onset Alzheimer's disease (DS-AD). Dysregulation of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) and insulin (INS) signaling pathways has been reported in DS. We hypothesized that upstream alterations in these two pathways contribute to hippocampal dysfunction in DS-AD.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This preliminary study investigates disruptions in upstream regulators of mTOR and insulin signaling pathways in the hippocampus of individuals with Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease neuropathology. The findings suggest that alterations in these pathways may contribute to hippocampal dysfunction in DS-AD, offering potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures. The authors found that these signatures are associated with prognosis and the immune landscape, suggesting lactylation plays a role in tumor progression and immunity in cervical cancer.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), revealing its association with vascular-immune crosstalk and its potential as a prognostic biomarker. The findings suggest EMCN may play a role in the tumor microenvironment and could be useful for patient stratification.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of ZNF695 in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma: single-cell and immune infiltration analyses.
papers.abstract: Zinc Finger Protein 695 (ZNF695) has been reported as a prognostic indicator in several cancers; however, its clinical implications and functional contributions within uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) have not yet been elucidated. Herein, the prognostic significance of ZNF695 in UCEC and its potential involvement in immune infiltration were examined.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of ZNF695 in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC), finding that its expression is associated with patient prognosis and immune cell infiltration. Using single-cell and immune infiltration analyses, the authors suggest ZNF695 could serve as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in UCEC.

papers.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm and astrocyte-associated diagnostic and therapeutic model for cirrhosis encephalopathy patients via integrative bioinformatic pipelines and in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: Cirrhosis encephalopathy (CE) is a severe neuropsychiatric complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by cognitive decline. While circadian rhythm (CR) disruption and astrocyte dysfunction are independently implicated, their integrated role in CE pathogenesis remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative bioinformatics and in vitro experiments to identify circadian rhythm and astrocyte-related genes as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets for cirrhosis encephalopathy, proposing a combined model that may improve patient stratification and treatment.

papers.title: Machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent vascular events in large, medium, or small vessels. These events contribute to cardiovascular disease primarily through thrombosis and atherosclerosis (AS). Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) represents a particularly high-risk manifestation of subclinical AS in patients with APS. However, the shared molecular signatures linking APS and CAS remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS). The findings reveal common molecular signatures that may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and provide insights into the shared pathophysiology of these conditions.

papers.title: TPI1 promotes malignant progression and ferroptosis resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Triosephosphate isomerase 1 (TPI1) is aberrantly overexpressed and exerts a critical oncogenic role in the development and progression of various human cancers by regulating multiple malignant biological phenotypes. However, the biological functions of TPI1 and the molecular mechanisms underlying its regulatory effect on ferroptosis sensitivity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remain not fully elucidated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of TPI1 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), finding that TPI1 is overexpressed and promotes malignant progression while conferring resistance to ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death. The findings suggest TPI1 as a potential therapeutic target in HNSCC.

papers.title: Neuronal precursor cell persistence in ganglioglioma is associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and immune cell infiltration.
papers.abstract: Gangliogliomas (GGs) are low-grade glioneuronal tumors that frequently present with drug-resistant epilepsy. Although their indolent course contrasts with their high epileptogenic potential, the oncogenic mechanisms sustaining neuronal precursor-like populations within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates gangliogliomas, low-grade brain tumors often associated with epilepsy, and finds that persistent neuronal precursor-like cells within the tumor are linked to extracellular matrix remodeling and immune cell infiltration. The findings suggest that the tumor microenvironment supports these precursor populations, potentially contributing to the tumor's unique epileptogenic properties.

papers.title: Aging-associated immune and stromal programs mark interferon- and remodeling-linked spatial contexts in psoriatic skin.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease characterized by spatially organized epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune interactions. Although aging is associated with inflammatory activation and tissue remodeling in skin, it remains unclear how aging-associated transcriptional programs are positioned within psoriatic tissue architecture and whether stromal cells with senescence-associated features retain inflammatory responsiveness.
papers.summary: This study maps aging-associated immune and stromal transcriptional programs within the spatial architecture of psoriatic skin, revealing that these programs are enriched in specific tissue contexts linked to interferon signaling and tissue remodeling. The findings suggest that senescent-like stromal cells in psoriatic lesions retain inflammatory responsiveness, potentially contributing to age-related exacerbation of psoriasis.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics and histopathological analyses reveal potential biomarkers and immune features linked to recurrence in head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: Head and neck cancers (HNCs) are aggressive malignancies, with recurrence contributing substantially to poor patient outcomes. We used spatial transcriptomics to identify tumour and immune features associated with recurrence.
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics to analyze head and neck cancer tumors, identifying specific tumor and immune features that are associated with disease recurrence. The findings reveal potential biomarkers and immune-related characteristics that could help predict which patients are at higher risk of recurrence, offering new avenues for improving prognosis and treatment strategies.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals the POSTN+ CAF-APOE+ macrophage axis drives immunosuppression and progression in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The progression of prostate cancer to lethal castration-resistant (CRPC) and metastatic (mCRPC) stages is driven by a profoundly remodeled tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the identity of key stromal cell populations, their developmental dynamics, and their precise crosstalk with immune cells remain incompletely understood, limiting our ability to target the TME therapeutically.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics to characterize the prostate cancer tumor microenvironment, identifying a specific axis between POSTN+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and APOE+ macrophages that drives immunosuppression and disease progression. The findings reveal a key stromal-immune crosstalk mechanism that could be targeted therapeutically in castration-resistant and metastatic prostate cancer.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Identification of UBE2C as a Prognostic Biomarker and Therapeutic Target Linked to Topotecan Sensitivity in Cervical Cancer.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma and endocervical adenocarcinoma (CESC) necessitate the discovery of novel biomarkers for prognostic and therapeutic advancement. This study aims to evaluate the clinical significance of ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2C (UBE2C) and its association with the tumor microenvironment (TME) in CESC. Methods: We meticulously sourced CESC data from renowned repositories such as The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx), and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), leveraging cutting-edge techniques including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-se
papers.summary: This study identifies UBE2C as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in cervical cancer by integrating multi-omics data from TCGA, GTEx, and GEO, including single-cell RNA sequencing. The findings suggest that UBE2C expression is associated with tumor microenvironment features and may predict sensitivity to the drug topotecan, offering a new avenue for patient stratification and treatment.

papers.title: UNC93B1 drives IL-6/STAT3-dependent tumor-macrophage crosstalk and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Lipid metabolic reprogramming is increasingly recognized as a driver of breast cancer progression; however, how lipid metabolism-associated risk states are translated into immune remodeling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) remains unclear. This study aimed to identify a lipid metabolism-related regulator that mediates tumor-macrophage crosstalk and to experimentally define its role in breast cancer progression.
papers.summary: This study identifies UNC93B1 as a lipid metabolism-related regulator that promotes breast cancer progression by driving IL-6/STAT3-dependent crosstalk between tumor cells and macrophages, which in turn induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The findings link lipid metabolic reprogramming to immune remodeling and EMT, providing a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell eQTL and multi-omics analyses reveal AIM1 and ANXA1 as immune-related hub genes and potential therapeutic targets in head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: Head and neck cancer (HNC) is characterized by substantial immune heterogeneity and limited availability of clinically actionable molecular targets. Here, we developed an integrative single-cell eQTL-driven multi-omics framework to identify immune cell-specific causal genes and prioritize drug-repurposing candidates for HNC.
papers.summary: This study presents an integrative framework combining single-cell eQTL and multi-omics data to identify immune-related hub genes in head and neck cancer, highlighting AIM1 and ANXA1 as potential therapeutic targets. The approach offers a strategy for prioritizing drug-repurposing candidates based on cell-type-specific causal genes.
